question: Do already expressed motor responses contain a transferable estimate of which review improves actual future actions, and can a small learned motor readout use them?
body: Uniform @8000 memory bodies, original 731–736 and independently initialized 811–816. All learned lifetime edits remain active. The readout study fixes inherited body parameters during the external selector fit to attribute effects to the readout.
physical_clock: Learn all ordinary objects, each once. The two offered objects are scanned in random order, both sensory orientations per object for five actual graph ticks each, without tasting or committing an edit. The graph's activity and eligibility traces advance through all 20 ticks. Record its native left/right motor logit at each actual view. Then show the same two-option physical review menu as the core experiment, choose a side and feed that native proprioception back to the same body. Recollect the chosen object, taste its actual payoff, perform a native write and answer. All methods use the exact same public scan, time, candidates and ordinary terminal draws.
controller: One tied four-hidden-unit tanh scorer of each offered object's two raw motor samples, plus one coefficient on the native menu logit. 17 learned real parameters shared across all bodies and both sides. The score difference modulates the final motor choice. This is an added readout with an explicit candidate binding and four transient recorded motor values; it is not credited as spontaneous computation by the unmodified graph. Neither input contains an absolute uncertainty, a true value or a gold review target.
training: Fit only on original six frozen bodies and separate generated training geometries (seed 1628301, four-object task, 768 per body). Each geometry crosses the two offered labels and an independent flip of the remaining label vector. Every executed continuation reveals only its actually obtained single terminal reward. Primary one-route dataset logs a fair random review choice, with known propensity .5 and one actual terminal payout per history. Optimize its importance-weighted expected payoff. A second, explicitly intervention-rich diagnostic fits both physically executed routes on the same histories. Common disjoint test seeds original 1628357 and independent 1628369, 384 worlds per load/cohort. No tuning on test and no refit for independent bodies. Fixed regularization, model width and fit iterations.
tests: Is the deployed readout better than same-body random, unassisted native, two-orientation hand uncertainty, and its own choices shuffled across private histories within identical geometry? Use actual physical sampled action plus expectation over the last route draw as a precision diagnostic. Check 2/4/8-object loads; four is primary. Also test the previous mixed-repair bodies without retraining the readout. Per-birth and paired crossed intervals.
